kept.spine: The town has taken the true measure of what it could not survive, and lets that measure govern what it dares to provoke.

kept.poolKey: Invasion & War: neither walls nor force
kept.spine: A drover finds nothing standing between the houses and the road here, and is asked at the first door what news he carries from behind him.
faces: A guard on the night round says he was given it street by street and left to guess at the rest.
At the tavern they give the reason there is no wall freely, and it comes out different at every table.
A clerk in the hall puts the want of a wall down to a want of money. He does not say what the money there is goes on.
The stallholders reckon the town's money here runs to the scales and the sweeping of the square.
A guild member says the trades could price a wall down to the carting. What they are asked for is money and never men.
Those who sit to hear a matter say nobody can put before them whether a line goes round the place, and they leave the question there.
The older heads here say what wants watching is the water, not any wall.
Whoever buries the dead says the ground for the dead is marked off and the rest of the place is not.

kept.spine: A quarrel between households here is settled between the households, and stays settled only as long as everyone who saw it still agrees that it was.
faces: A pedlar reports that a dispute over a debt here is argued out at the door where it started, and settled nowhere else.
One of the elders says a household may settle what it likes on its own, but whatever is brought to the elders is settled their way.
At the tavern they say the households which do the settling are the ones with the most fields, and the drinkers can name them.

A woman old enough to remember the custom says a boundary between two households is walked and argued over until both sides agree. The walking is done by the households themselves, in time neither one has to spare.
The muster says it is expected to stand behind whatever the households decide and is not asked first.
A quarrel that starts inside is none of the gate's, whoever keeps the gate says, and a quarrel that starts at the gate is settled at the gate.
Whoever digs the ground says they are told when to dig and not what was decided, and they do not ask.

kept.spine: What any common arrangement here would cost, and which household would carry it, has never been settled.
faces: A household's store is in its own cellar and under its own floor, a stranger says. The neighbours know which floor covers what and say as much to a visitor.
Those who keep the ground say a burying is the one thing here that waits for no purse.
The households that keep the custom hold that even a household with nothing else to give still finds what a burial costs, when it comes to that.
It is the same backs that come out, they say at the tavern. Everyone at the table can name the ones who stay behind their own door.
The muster says the ground it would gather on is somebody's own field, and that somebody would bear the trampling of the crop.
Those who hold the way through reckon nobody set the hour the bar comes down, and the hour follows the light.
The shortfall comes off the stalls, they say at the market, and the argument comes from behind every stall.
The soldiers say the place says plainly what it wants of them. The people here ask them straight out to put a shoulder to a load.

kept.poolKey: Disasters & Famine: NO reserves, NO medical provision
kept.spine: It is common knowledge here that there is no grain store to turn to and no house set aside for the sick, and the town has never counted either as a want.
faces: One of the elders says a household with someone sick in it is never left to manage alone.
At the tavern they say the houses that are sat up with are the houses that sit up with others.
A rider who stopped a night here reports that a sick house is known from the lane by the food left on its step.
At the market they say a house with somebody ill in it comes for vinegar and roots, and whoever has them names the price.
Those who bury the dead reckon they are the one trade here that is sent for in a bad year and not thanked for coming.

kept.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
kept.spine: This is a first reading of Warmholz's safety, honest about what has been seen and silent about what has not.
No criminal structure has been identified at Warmholz. Whatever wrongdoing exists here does not answer to anything that could be called an organization.
A traveller can come into Warmholz from any direction that suits him, and is stopped by nobody on the way in.
A carter at Warmholz can find nobody whose job the town's defense is, because it is nobody's job at all.

kept.poolKey: charter hall ABSENT where the country warrants one
kept.spine: No charter hall stands at Warmholz where the country's own law calls for one, and whatever must be done in its place falls to hands that were never suited for it, at a cost paid every time.
Nothing unseen has come at Warmholz, and nothing here would know if it had. What counts as safe and what could actually be detected are two different things.
Warmholz is too small to wall, and it knows it. Its safety is its neighbours, its distance and its unimportance.
No food buffer exists at Warmholz. Any break in supply becomes a matter of survival within days, not seasons.
